briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for July 31, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 The Gravity of the Global Climate Crisis
sections.content: Today's news once again highlights the severity of the climate crisis facing the world. Record low water levels in major European waterways have led to the shutdown of nuclear power plants on the Danube River, which has reached its lowest level in decades [1, 80]. In France and Spain, human-induced climate change has increased the likelihood of wildfires by up to 20 times [58, 60], resulting in the evacuation of hundreds of thousands of people and widespread destruction [82]. In the UK, this summer's heatwave fatalities are expected to be the highest on record [8, 83]. Domestically, as nationwide heatwaves and tropical nights persist [21], the Korea Environment Institute (KEI) has warned about the dangers of heatwaves [7]. The climate crisis is thus ongoing and accelerating [51], leading the Vice-President of the European Union to express concern that Europe is 'unprepared' for the impacts of climate change [42].

sections.title: ⚠️ Complex Threats and Vulnerabilities Caused by Climate Change
sections.content: Climate change poses complex threats across our lives and ecosystems. In Osan City, South Korea, the activity of infectious disease vectors has increased due to climate change [3]. Furthermore, with intensifying heatwaves, cooling emissions are projected to triple by 2050, exacerbating the 'climate paradox' [4]. Additionally, seedling data from Michigan forests show stress on forests due to climate change, deer, and disease [39]. Disturbances to natural ecosystems are accelerating, with Himalayan rivers changing their courses more rapidly [47]. In the agricultural sector, difficulties due to climate change are also growing, including threats to corn production [70] and challenges in blackcurrant cultivation [76]. Seosan City Council member Lee Man emphasized preparedness for complex disasters caused by the climate crisis [10].

sections.title: 🌱 Transition to Carbon Neutrality and Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Amidst these threats, global efforts to address climate change and transition to a carbon-neutral society continue steadily. Domestically, Yeongju City is expanding the demonstration of new horticultural crop varieties and disseminating agricultural technologies [2]. Chungju City is introducing additional eco-friendly hydrogen buses [12], demonstrating active local-level adaptation and mitigation efforts. LocknLock has significantly improved its greenhouse gas reduction performance by linking CEO and executive bonuses to carbon reduction targets [5]. The Chungbuk Institute of Science and Technology Innovation is supporting technological innovation by recruiting companies to participate in its Carbon Neutral Technology Living Lab [13]. Internationally, Vietnam has allocated over 337 billion VND to infrastructure and urban development projects for climate change adaptation [9]. Germany's wind and solar power generation has surpassed fossil fuels for the first time ever [19], accelerating the expansion of renewable energy and the transition to carbon neutrality [17, 14].

sections.title: 🌍 Call for Climate Action and Raising Awareness
sections.content: Policy efforts and public awareness-raising to address the climate crisis are also emerging as crucial tasks. In Putnam County, public feedback is being gathered on the Climate Change Adaptation and Resilience Plan (CCARP) [32]. Democratic insiders are advocating for a focus on climate change in relation to 'Project 2029' [43]. Movements urging responsible action are also emerging, such as the City of Boulder's intention to pursue climate change litigation against oil and gas companies [46]. Meanwhile, the general public tends to underestimate support for climate action and overestimate the actual actions of others [85], which highlights the importance of accurate information dissemination and communication. Furthermore, rebuttals against attempts by some climate skeptics to share misinformation are continuing [86].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the reality of the climate crisis and the various efforts being made to combat it. Climate change is no longer a distant threat but a reality we face today, and emphasizing that only sustained attention and proactive action can create a better future, I conclude today's climate briefing.
